lessons.notes: Unit 1 has a prose lesson (The Lighthouse, p. 1–13) and a poem (The Rainbow, p. 14–16). Remember: a trip is a short visit to some place, after which you return home. A journey means going from one place to another over a long distance. To travel means to go from place to place. A voyage is a long journey by sea or air.
ab: Preparatory Activity – 1a Discuss in pairs: useful inventions made by scientists (p. 1)
Discuss in pairs: What are some of the useful inventions made by scientists? How useful are these inventions?

ಸೂಚಿತ ಉತ್ತರ:
Electric light – helps us to see and work at night.
Telephone – helps us to talk to people who live far away.
Computer – helps us to write, calculate and learn quickly.
Television – gives us news, cartoons and learning programmes.
Medicines – cure our diseases.
Bicycle – helps us to travel without using petrol.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
Preparatory Activity – 1b What would our life be like without inventions? (p. 1)
the electric light
We would have to study in the dark. (ಪುಸ್ತಕದ ಉದಾಹರಣೆ)
the telephone
We could not talk quickly to our relatives and friends who live far away.
the computer
We would have to do all our writing and calculations by hand and it would take a lot of time.
the bicycle
We would have to walk long distances to go to school or to the market.
the television
We could not watch news, cartoons and other programmes at home.
the medicines
Sick people would not get cured and many diseases would spread.
the plastic material
We would have to use heavy things made of glass, metal or wood for our buckets, bottles and toys.
the X-ray
Doctors could not easily find a broken bone or a problem inside our body.
Preparatory Activity – 2 Words that come to your mind when you hear the word 'lighthouse' (p. 1)
Make a list of all the words that come to your mind when you hear the word 'lighthouse'. Read out the list to the class. Find out who has written the maximum number of words.

ಸೂಚಿತ ಪದಗಳು: sea, ship, boat, sailor, fisherman, tower, light, shore, rocks, waves, night, fire, guide, warning, safety, electricity.

Let's Understand – C1 Discuss in pairs and answer the following questions (p. 4)
Why was Rajiv thrilled?
Rajiv was thrilled because his father was going to take him out on a visit to the lighthouse.
What is a lighthouse?
A lighthouse is a tall, strong building in the shape of a tower with powerful lights at the top.
How are lighthouses useful to sailors?
Lighthouses help the sailors to know where the land is and what place they are near. They warn and guide the sailors in places which are dangerous to ships.
Where are the lighthouses built?
Lighthouses are built on the seashore and sometimes in the sea, in places which are dangerous to ships.
What did the people use in lighthouses before the invention of electricity?
Before electricity, wood fires were lit in high places on the shore. Later, a large number of candles with glass around them (to keep out the wind) were used.
How was the first lighthouse built?

Many fishermen were lost in the sea and could not return home. A group of clever young men collected a few huge logs and lots of dry branches and set fire to them. They kept the fire burning even though the elders laughed at them. Next morning the fishermen sailed home, guided by the light of that fire.
Find words, from the story, which mean the opposite of the following: i. dangerous  ii. short  iii. far  iv. low  v. old  vi. stop
dangerous – safe; short – tall; far – near; low – high; old – young (modern ಎಂದೂ ಬರೆಯಬಹುದು); stop – start

lessons.t: Unit 2 · The Scholar's Mother Tongue (ವಿದ್ವಾಂಸನ ಮಾತೃಭಾಷೆ)
lessons.words: scholar – someone who has studied a subject and knows a lot about it; court – (ಆಸ್ಥಾನ); fluent – able to use a language naturally without stopping or making mistakes; sneak – go quietly; whisper – speak in a low voice; tickle – touch someone lightly; astonished – surprised; dismay – a feeling of sadness and disappointment; depressed – in great pain or sadness; grief – deep sorrow; cold – unfriendly; kindly – kind and caring; erect – straight; charity – kindness or sympathy; want – poverty; bind – tie a long thin piece of fabric around something; far – very much
lessons.notes: Unit 2 has a prose lesson (The Scholar's Mother Tongue, p. 17–31) and a poem (Sympathy by Charles Mackay, p. 32–36). Answers to the riddles are given by the book on p. 31.
ab: Preparatory Activity – 1 Can you answer the following riddles? (p. 17)
What is the longest word in the English language?
Smiles – because there is a 'mile' between its first and last letters.
What starts with 'P', ends with 'E' and has millions of letters?
The Post office.
What word begins with 'e', ends with 'e' and has one letter?
Envelope.
Which 'pillar' keeps crawling all the time?
Caterpillar.
What has size and shape but no weight?
A shadow.
Which son may prove dangerous?
Poison.
What cannot move or walk, but can go from place to place?
A road.
Which letter in the English alphabet always asks a question?
Y (why).
Preparatory Activity – 2 Puzzle: Akbar's line (p. 17)
One day Akbar drew a line on the floor and commanded, 'Make this line shorter but don't by any means erase any part of it.' When it was Birbal's turn, he at once ……(what did Birbal do?)……
Birbal drew a longer line next to the first one, without touching the first line. So the first line became shorter in comparison.
Let's Understand – C1 Answer the following questions in one or two sentences each (p. 25)
Who was the visitor at Akbar's court one day?
A learned scholar (Pandit) was the visitor at Akbar's court.
What did he tell the king and courtiers?
He told them that he had mastery over different languages and could speak many languages fluently.
What did he challenge the court?
He challenged the court to find out what his mother tongue was.
What did Birbal tickle the Pandit's ear with?
Birbal tickled the Pandit's ear with a feather.
Was Pandit's mother tongue Hindi? Mention his mother tongue.
No, the Pandit's mother tongue was not Hindi. His mother tongue was Telugu.
Let's Understand – C2 Say whether the following statements are True or False (p. 25)
A learned scholar once visits the court of Jahangir.
False. (A learned scholar once visited the court of Akbar.)
Birbal says he can speak many languages.
False. (The Pandit says he can speak many languages.)
Birbal tickles Pandit's ear with a feather.
True.
The Pandit admits his defeat.
True.
Let's Understand – C3 Rearrange the sentences to make the story meaningful (pp. 25–26)
The paragraph below is the story you have just read. Rearrange the sentences a–f to make it meaningful. Do it in pairs.

The correct order is: c – b – d – f – a – e
(c) A learned Pandit once visited the court of Akbar. He told the King that he had mastery over different languages.
(b) The Pandit could speak many languages fluently. He challenged everybody at the court to name his mother tongue.
(d) Everyone in the court failed; the challenge was taken up by Birbal.
(f) Birbal quietly entered into the Pandit's bedroom and tickled his ear with a feather. Pandit, half awake, shouted out words in his mother tongue.
(a) Birbal came to the court the next day and told everyone that the Pandit's mother tongue was Telugu.
(e) The King questioned how he knew this and Birbal narrated the incident that took place in the Pandit's bedroom.
Let's Understand – C4 Titles and Birbal's way (p. 26)
The title of the story is "The Scholar's Mother Tongue". Work with your partner and think of some other suitable titles.

ಸೂಚಿತ ಶೀರ್ಷಿಕೆಗಳು: Birbal's Wit; The Clever Birbal; The Pandit's Challenge; A Feather and a Language.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
Suppose you are Birbal in the story. Write a few sentences on (a) how you would find out the scholar's mother tongue, (b) what you would use to tickle the Pandit's ear with other than a feather.

ಮಾದರಿ:
(a) I would go to the Pandit's room at night when he is fast asleep. I would whisper a few words and wait for him to talk in his sleep. A sleeping person speaks in his mother tongue.
(b) I would use a small piece of cotton (or a thin blade of grass).
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
Let's Speak – Narrate the story of Akbar and Birbal using the clues (p. 26)

One day Akbar asked the courtiers ... what punishment to be given to the person who pulled his beard ... courtiers ... different opinions ... to kill under the feet of elephant ... Akbar got bored ... asked Birbal ... Birbal said ... you should offer sweets ... courtiers surprised ... Akbar pleased ... asked Birbal the reason ... Birbal explained ... none other than the prince would be bold enough to touch his beard ... Akbar rewarded him.

ಸೂಚಿತ ನಿರೂಪಣೆ:
One day Akbar asked the courtiers what punishment should be given to the person who pulled his beard. The courtiers gave different opinions. Some said, "He should be killed under the feet of an elephant." Akbar got bored with their answers and asked Birbal. Birbal said, "You should offer him sweets." The courtiers were surprised, but Akbar was pleased and asked Birbal the reason. Birbal explained that none other than the prince would be bold enough to touch the king's beard. Akbar rewarded him.
ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.

How did the proud man react to the poet's sorrow?
The proud man heard the poet's grief and gave him gold, but his looks were cold and he did not say even a single kind word.

It means that the proud man looked at the poet in an unfriendly way. He showed no kindness or sympathy.
In spite of having gold, the poor man was not happy. Why?

According to the poet, heavenly sympathy (kindness) is greater than gold.

The poet says that gold is valuable, but sympathy is much more valuable. Money can be paid back, but the loving care of the poor man cannot be repaid.

Sugar, proteins, iron and calcium.
Why do bees fan honey?

Where do bees store the honey?
In honeycombs.
What is a honeycomb?
A block of wax full of six-sided holes in which bees store honey.
How long does a honey bee live?
A honey bee does not live longer than a month.
Read the lesson again and write two things that the bees do to produce honey.

Any two: (1) Bees visit flowers and collect nectar. (2) They store the nectar in their honey sacs and carry it to the beehive. (3) They drop the honey into honeycombs. (4) They fan their wings to thicken the honey. (5) They cap the honeycomb with wax.
Mention the work done by the house bees and field bees.
House bees keep the house clean and well ventilated, and build new combs to store honey. Field bees are older bees; they go out of the house to search for nectar.

ಮಾದರಿ: I visit flowers and suck the nectar with my long tongue. I store it in my honey sac and carry it to the beehive. There the nectar turns into honey. I drop the honey into the honeycomb, fan my wings to thicken it and cap the comb with wax.

Let's Understand – C1 Answer each question briefly (pp. 62–63)
Who did the lion make his Home Minister and why?
The fox, because he was very wise and clever.
Who was made the Defence Minister and why?
The leopard, because he was very alert and swift-footed.
Why was the crow made the Minister for External Affairs?
Because he can fly high in the sky (and see far).
What promise did the three ministers make to the king?
They swore to remain loyal to the king.
What did the king promise to do for his ministers?
He promised to give them food and protection.
How did the ministers always have enough to eat?
They helped the lion find prey, and after having his fill he left the remains for them.
What did the crow tell the lion about the camel?
The crow said camel meat is very tasty and that he had seen a lone camel in the desert, which looked fat and big.
Who brought the camel to the lion and how?
The fox brought the camel. He lied to the camel that the lion had killed his cruel master and invited him to live in the forest.
Why did the lion feel grateful to the camel?
The camel carried the lion, the fox, the leopard and the crow back to the forest when they were tired and hungry, so he saved the lion's life.
Why did the lion ask his ministers to get him some food?
Because he was tired and hungry, and his paws were badly burnt, so he could not hunt by himself.
Who do you think proved most faithful to the king?
The camel proved most faithful; he was willing to live with the lion, and he was not tempted to harm the king. ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.

Were the three ministers loyal to the lion? Give reasons.
They seemed loyal, because they offered to be eaten. But they were not truly loyal – they wanted the camel for food, and they ran away when the lion said he would eat them.
Why did the three ministers run away from the place?
They ran away because they did not want to be eaten by the lion, and the lion had said he would eat them in the order they offered themselves.

Let's Understand – C1 Answer in one or two sentences each (pp. 79–80)
Where did the disciples of Dronacharya assemble for the test?
In the large open ground in front of the Hastinapura palace.
What was the target set up by the Guru?
An artificial bird (made of wood and grass) set on top of a branch of a tree.
What was Yudhishtira's reply when Drona asked him what he saw on the tree?
He said, "I can see the tree, the bird, my brothers, other friends and everything."
Was Drona happy with the answers given by many of the princes? Why / why not?
No. Most princes said they could see only the tree or the branch, or everything. Drona wanted them to focus only on the bird, so he was not pleased.
Who passed this test?
Arjuna.
Why did Drona ask Arjuna to shoot the bird?
Because Arjuna could see only the bird and its neck and head – he was focused, so Drona allowed him to shoot.
Who didn't congratulate Arjuna on his achievement? Why?
Duryodhana did not congratulate Arjuna, because he was jealous.
What happened when Drona was washing his feet one day?
A crocodile caught hold of his foot while he was washing it on the side of a stream.
Who drove the crocodile away? How?
Arjuna drove the crocodile away by shooting an arrow into the stream at the right point.
Who do you think was the most favourite disciple of Drona? Why?
Arjuna, because he showed focus, skill and quick action. ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಆಧರಿಸಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುವುದು.
What is important to succeed in life?
Concentration and focus, dexterity, and prompt and proper responsive action.
Let's Understand – C2 Discuss in small groups and answer (p. 80)

Drona asked each prince to shoot the bird on top of the tree, after asking him what he could see. Yudhishtira said he could see everything, so Drona did not allow him to shoot. Only Arjuna, who could see only the bird's neck and head, was allowed to shoot.
How did Arjuna prove his skill in archery?
Arjuna shot an arrow and hit the bird's neck; the bird fell down. Later he shot an arrow into the stream and drove the crocodile away.
